sections.h2: What should I ask on a Thanksgiving catering call?
sections.body:
Thanksgiving catering orders are not like a regular pickup order. You need the basics fast, but you also need enough detail to avoid confusion later.

Use a short script like: "Thanks for calling. Is this for pickup or delivery, and what day and time do you need it ready?" Then move straight into the food count.

**Checklist for every catering call:**
- Caller name and best callback number
- Pickup or delivery
- Event date and ready time
- Number of people or trays needed
- Menu items, sizes, and modifiers
- Allergies or special notes
- Payment method your restaurant already accepts

For a catering call, it helps to confirm the big items in the caller’s words. Example: "So I have two full trays of baked ziti, one tray of chicken cutlets, and 20 rolls for Thursday at 3:30. Is that right?" If the caller wants something custom or allergy-sensitive, ROAL can hand that to staff instead of guessing.

sections.h2: How do I keep Thanksgiving catering orders from getting lost?
sections.body:
The problem is usually not the phone call itself. It is where the order goes after the call ends.

Use one place for every catering request. That can be a kitchen screen, a written prep sheet, or a dashboard your team checks first thing. ROAL sends a clean ticket to the kitchen screen, which helps turn a call into something the kitchen can read quickly.

A simple workflow looks like this:
1. Answer the phone with a holiday greeting.
2. Take the catering details.
3. Repeat the order back.
4. Confirm the ready time.
5. Send it to the kitchen and note any special instructions.

**Example order ticket fields:**
| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| Name | Maria S. |
| Phone | (555) 123-4567 |
| Date | Thanksgiving Eve |
| Ready time | 4:00 PM |
| Items | 3 trays pasta, 2 salads, 4 desserts |
| Notes | No nuts, call on arrival |

That kind of format saves time when the line is busy and the staff member picking up the order did not take the call.

sections.h2: What do I say when callers want prices or a custom menu?
sections.body:
Thanksgiving catering callers often ask for pricing before they know exactly what they want. Keep your answer short, then guide them to the next step.

Try this line: "I can help with that. Tell me how many people you’re feeding, and I’ll go item by item." If your menu has set trays or holiday packages, read those first. If you do not have set packages, quote by the item and the count.

Here is a practical way to think about it:
- Say a $28 average item or tray price, if that is close to your menu.
- If the caller wants 6 trays, that is about $168 before any extras.
- If your own tray price is different, plug in your number.

If the caller asks for something you cannot answer quickly, do not stall the line. Send it to staff with a note. ROAL is built to answer from the restaurant’s live menu and pass questions it cannot answer into an inbox, so the owner can reply once and the host knows it from then on.

For pricing on the tool itself, see [Pricing](/pricing).

sections.h2: How can I handle Thanksgiving calls when the phone is already ringing?
sections.body:
Holiday phone traffic usually hits when the kitchen is busy, the front counter is moving, and nobody has time to sit through a long catering call. That is when missed calls become lost orders.

You do not need a huge setup. You need a backup plan that works when staff is tied up.

Use this practical setup:
- Keep your restaurant number.
- Forward calls when busy or unanswered.
- Make sure the caller hears your normal business details.
- Test the forwarding before the holiday week.

US phone forwarding codes vary by carrier and plan, so confirm with your provider and test with a real call. On many landlines and some carriers, `*72` forwards all calls and `*73` turns it off. Some mobile carriers use codes such as `**21*number#` for all calls and `##21#` to stop it; some support busy and no-answer forwarding too. Business VoIP systems usually handle it in the web portal.

If you want a quick refresher, use [Call forwarding codes by carrier](/tools/call-forwarding-codes) and test after setup.

sections.h2: How much does one missed Thanksgiving catering call cost me?
sections.body:
You do not need a perfect number to see the risk. You just need a working example.

Say a catering order would have been $180. If two calls like that were missed during a holiday afternoon, that is $360 in potential order value. If your real average catering ticket is higher or lower, swap in your own number.

Here is another way to look at it:
| Example | Number |
|---|---|
| Average catering order | $180 |
| Missed calls on a busy day | 3 |
| Possible lost order value | $540 |

That does not include the time spent calling back, or the chance the customer found another restaurant before you returned the call. Many restaurants also pay for answering help in ways that charge by the minute or by the call, while some AI phone tools charge a monthly fee whether or not orders come in. ROAL uses a per-completed-order model: $0.90 for a confirmed order whose ticket reaches the kitchen screen, with no monthly fee, no setup fee, and no per-minute fee.

faq.q: What should I ask on a Thanksgiving catering call?
faq.a: Ask for the caller’s name, callback number, event date, ready time, pickup or delivery, guest count, menu items, sizes, modifiers, and any allergy notes. Then repeat the order back in one sentence before ending the call. That keeps small mistakes from turning into a bad holiday pickup.
